note: Weather round before you fly. Rome is dry and near 80 through Monday, then Tuesday Oct 6 is a washout (about an inch), so that is the Vatican day. Bologna is overcast but mostly dry; Verona Friday is cool and clear, 49 to 67. No thumbs or notes yet, so nothing dropped. Added Sunday-proof Rome tables (Velavevodetto ai Quiriti, Piccolo Arancio, Felice), a Verona tower and Amarone bar for after Perbellini, and Mercato Albinelli for Modena. Palatium now trades as VyNIQUE; Sunday hours still unconfirmed, so use Terre e Domus on Sundays.

days.2026-10-02: Travel day. Rome will be dry and near 80 through Monday, with one wet Tuesday, so pack a light rain layer. Sleep on the plane; tomorrow's dinner at Trattoria Cacio e Pepe is a short walk from the NYX.
days.2026-10-03: Clear and about 80 when you land. Drop bags at the NYX, walk to Castel Sant'Angelo and along the river at sunset, then dinner at Trattoria Cacio e Pepe near the hotel. Order the cacio e pepe and ask for a Frascati. Keep it early; the jet lag wins tonight.
days.2026-10-04: Sunny, 79, your first Rome Sunday. Forno Campo de' Fiori, Da Oio, Supplizio, Il Goccetto and Cacio e Pepe are shut. Morning on the car-free Via Appia Antica, lunch at Velavevodetto ai Quiriti near the NYX (open daily; book), then Terre e Domus by Trajan's Column for Lazio wine. The Pantheon is free today, so expect a line or save it for Oct 11.
days.2026-10-05: Overcast but dry and 79, the last dry day in Rome. Testaccio day: Mercato Testaccio (open Mondays to 3:30) or Felice a Testaccio for lunch, Castel Sant'Angelo at 2 pm for 5 euros, then dinner at Da Oio a Casa Mia for the gricia. Book Da Oio. Save the Vatican for tomorrow's rain.
days.2026-10-06: Rain most of the day, close to an inch, 65 to 71. Vatican Museums with online tickets (New Wing shuts at 1 pm), Bonci Pizzarium after, then a long stop at Il Goccetto or Palatium for Frascati and Cesanese. Try for Armando al Pantheon at dinner. Pack tonight for the 9:10 train.
days.2026-10-07: 9:10 train, Bologna by 11:33, partly cloudy and 71, dry. Check into the NH; I Famosi Tortellini della Nonna is on your walk into town. Afternoon in the Quadrilatero: Paolo Atti, then salumi to Osteria del Sole for Pignoletto. Dinner at Trattoria di Via Serra near the station; book it.
days.2026-10-08: Pasta class and lunch at 10. Cloudy, 71, a chance of a late shower, so stay central after: the Archiginnasio anatomy theater, coffee at Caffe Terzi, gelato at Cremeria Santo Stefano. Keep dinner light: Enoteca Italiana for Lambrusco di Sorbara and cheese, or a Mo! mortadella roll.
days.2026-10-09: Verona: cool and clear, 49 to 67, so bring a layer. Lunch at Casa Perbellini 12 Apostoli at 12:45; take a morning train and walk Piazza delle Erbe first. After lunch, climb Torre dei Lamberti, then Amarone by the glass at Antica Bottega del Vino. Evening train back; Osteria del Sole stays open late.
days.2026-10-10: Overcast and dry, 68 to 71. Morning train to Modena: Mercato Albinelli (Saturday to 7 pm) for Parmigiano, balsamic and a glass of Grasparossa, then the Duomo. Dinner at Al Gatto Verde at 7:30; check how far it is from Modena station and line up a taxi. Want Bologna first? All'Osteria Bottega does lunch; book.
days.2026-10-11: 11:12 train, Rome by 1:35, mostly clear, 75, maybe a sprinkle. Check in at the Je, then the Pantheon (no first-Sunday crowd now) and a gran caffe at Sant'Eustachio. Sunset loop on the Aventine for the keyhole. Sunday dinner: Armando is shut, so Piccolo Arancio by Trevi (book) or Poldo e Gianna, then Giolitti.
days.2026-10-12: 10:30 flight from FCO, a dry morning. Leave the Je by 7. If you are up early, one last espresso at Sant'Eustachio, a short walk from the hotel.

items.name: Da Oio a Casa Mia
items.why: Order the gricia, the signature pasta, in a loud AS Roma-themed trattoria; reserve ahead.
items.quote: Da Oio is a classic Roman trattoria.

items.name: Forno Campo de' Fiori
items.why: Pizza bianca and filled slices sold by weight; an easy walk-around lunch off the piazza.
items.quote: Open: Monday – Saturday from 7:30 am to 2:30 pm

items.name: Trattoria Cacio e Pepe
items.why: Cacio e pepe made the old way with Pecorino Romano; carbonara and amatriciana too. Close to the NYX.
items.quote: made the old-fashioned way with Pecorino Romano and black pepper

items.name: Armando al Pantheon
items.why: Family-run Roman classics beside the Pantheon; one of the hardest tables in town, so book dinner early.
items.quote: Just make sure to book your visit in advance

items.name: Poldo e Gianna Osteria
items.why: Roman dishes with a modern twist and a strong wine list, a short walk from the Je Rome.
items.quote: Its cuisine draws on Roman traditions, reinterpreted with modern techniques

items.name: Bonci Pizzarium
items.why: Crispy pizza al taglio by weight; try the fried eggplant slice and the polpette di bollito.
items.quote: Pizzarium has the best pizza al taglio in Rome

items.name: Supplizio
items.why: Chef Dandini's supplì, fried rice balls, from classic to cacio e pepe, about 3 euros each.
items.quote: to enjoy all the flavors of the traditional Roman street food

items.name: VyNIQUE Enoteca Regionale del Lazio (ex Palatium)
items.why: Lazio-only wine bar, now branded VyNIQUE; ask for Frascati or Cesanese by the glass. Sunday hours unconfirmed.
items.quote: Enoteca Regionale del Lazio Via Frattina 94, Roma

items.name: Terre e Domus (Enoteca della Provincia di Roma)
items.why: The Rome province's enoteca facing Trajan's Column; local Lazio wine and food only, open all day.
items.quote: Terre e Domus has only local specialities on offer

items.name: Il Goccetto
items.why: Cult enoteca with up to 20 wines by the glass; ask the bar to pour a Lazio white or red.
items.quote: ideal place to come if you are looking to try lots of regional wines

items.name: Caffè Sant'Eustachio
items.why: Roman institution roasting its own blend; the gran caffè, a sweetened espresso, is the house order.
items.quote: Their signature blend is made from 100% Arabica beans

items.name: Giolitti
items.why: Gelato and pastries since 1900 in a Liberty-style room; an easy dessert stop near the Je.
items.quote: Dal 1900, il gusto della tradizione dolciaria italiana

items.name: Vatican Museums
items.why: Sistine Chapel and miles of galleries, good in rain. Buy tickets online; the New Wing closes at 1 pm Oct 6.
items.quote: From Monday to Saturday 08.00 a.m. – 08.00 p.m.

items.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
items.why: Papal fortress with Tiber views. Free Sun Oct 4; open Mon Oct 5, 2 to 8 pm, for 5 euros, no booking.
items.quote: La prenotazione del biglietto è raccomandata tutti i giorni

items.name: Pantheon
items.why: Open daily 9 to 7. Entry is free on the first Sunday of the month, which is Oct 4, so expect a queue.
items.quote: La prima domenica di ogni mese l'ingresso al Pantheon è gratuito.

items.name: Mercato Testaccio
items.why: Covered food market with ready-to-eat stalls; open Mon to Sat, 7 to 3:30, so Monday lunch before Da Oio works.
items.quote: Open 07:00-15:30. Closed Sun.

items.name: Via Appia Antica on a Sunday
items.why: Walk or bike the ancient road on Sunday Oct 4, when it is closed to cars; the info point rents bikes.
items.quote: The Appian Way is closed to the traffic on Sundays and holidays

items.name: Aventine Hill loop: roses, oranges, keyhole
items.why: Free hilltop loop to the Knights of Malta keyhole framing St. Peter's dome; a good Oct 11 afternoon walk.
items.quote: Peeking through the Aventine Keyhole is free

items.name: Trattoria Anna Maria
items.why: Classic trattoria for tagliatelle al ragù and tortellini in brodo. Closed Monday and Tuesday lunch.
items.quote: Tagliatelle al ragù Tortellini in brodo Passatelli in brodo

items.name: All'Osteria Bottega
items.why: Tiny, much-loved osteria: tortellini in brodo, tagliatelle with Medicina onions and a cured-meat plate. Reserve ahead.
items.quote: it's one of Bologna's most in-demand tables and the room is small

items.name: Trattoria di Via Serra
items.why: Michelin Bib Gourmand trattoria just north of the station: tortellini in broth, zuppa inglese. Lunch Tue-Sat; book.
items.quote: excellent tortellini in broth

items.name: Paolo Atti & Figli (Quadrilatero)
items.why: Market-street stop: fresh tortellini and tigelle at Atti, then browse the nearby salumerie for mortadella. Go before 11am.
items.quote: has been selling fresh pasta and traditional bread from Via Drapperie since 1868

items.name: Mò! Mortadella Lab
items.why: Takeaway mortadella rolls; a quick rain-day lunch or snack to pair with a glass of Pignoletto nearby.
items.quote: L’inimitabile street food di rosette con la mortadella

items.name: Mercato delle Erbe
items.why: Covered market with produce, cured meats, cheese and wine stalls; a dry place to graze for lunch.
items.quote: It is closed on Sundays.

items.name: I Famosi Tortellini della Nonna
items.why: Historic pasta shop on the main street from the station: fresh tortellini, mortadella, cheese. Shut Sunday; Thursday afternoon.
items.quote: From 1949 a little shop which sells fresh pasta and typical products from Bologna.

items.name: Osteria del Sole
items.why: Wine-only osteria since 1465: bring salumi from the Quadrilatero and drink local wine at long wooden tables.
items.quote: Here, no food is served, but everyone can bring their own.

items.name: Enoteca Italiana
items.why: Wine shop and bar with about 2,000 labels; ask for Pignoletto or Albana, with cured meats and cheese.
items.quote: focus on local wines like Pignoletto or Albana

items.name: Enoteca Storica Faccioli
items.why: Historic enoteca with Emilia-Romagna own-label wines and a Romagna Albana; walk-ins only, opens 4pm Mon-Wed.
items.quote: No reservation required, only walks in.

items.name: Caffè Terzi
items.why: Roaster-run espresso bar two minutes from the Two Towers; order an espresso or cappuccino and a pastry.
items.quote: Espresso and cappuccino are the most demanded

items.name: Cremeria Santo Stefano
items.why: Top-rated gelato shop; pistachio, hazelnut or stracciatella, a good stop after the Santo Stefano churches. Closed Mon, Tue.
items.quote: Lunedì Chiusa Martedì Chiusa

items.name: Archiginnasio and Anatomical Theatre
items.why: The old university palace with a carved wooden anatomy theater; an indoor rain-day stop. Closed Sundays.
items.quote: a wooden room carved by Antonio Levante in 1637 for anatomical teaching

items.name: Due Torri (Asinelli and Garisenda)
items.why: Asinelli climb is closed and Garisenda is being restored, so admire them from the street; the Clock Tower climb is the alternative.
items.quote: ASINELLI TOWER IS CLOSED FOR AREA MAINTAINANCE

items.name: Santo Stefano (Sette Chiese)
items.why: Cluster of linked medieval churches and cloisters around a quiet piazza; mostly indoors. Closed Mondays; limited during services.
items.quote: Santo Stefano is the most unique complex in Bologna

items.name: Portico di San Luca walk
items.why: 3.8 km covered portico of 666 arches uphill to the sanctuary; about 45-60 min up, dry in showers. Go on a clear day.
items.quote: The portico protects you from weather but not from the grade.

items.name: Modena (Lambrusco country)
items.why: About 30 min by train. Go early on Saturday before the Al Gatto Verde dinner: Mercato Albinelli, the Duomo, a glass of Lambrusco.
items.quote: Trains from Bologna Centrale to Modena take an average of 30 minutes

items.name: Ravenna mosaics
items.why: Byzantine mosaics, mostly indoors; roughly 1-2 hours by regional train, sources differ. Time-slot tickets; drink Romagna Sangiovese.
items.quote: Every day 9.00-19.00 last admission 18.30

items.name: Velavevodetto ai Quiriti
items.why: Roman trattoria open every day, lunch 12:30 to 2:30 and dinner 7:30 to 10:30; your Sunday Oct 4 fix near the NYX.
items.quote: Pranzo (dal Lunedì alla Domenica) 12:30–14:30 Cena (dal Lunedì alla Domenica) 19:30–22:30

items.name: Piccolo Arancio
items.why: Family trattoria steps from Trevi, open Sunday night when Armando is shut; gricia, cacio e pepe, carciofo alla giudia.
items.quote: Closed on Mondays Open Tuesday through Sunday: 12:00 to 15:30 / 18:30 to 24:00

items.name: Felice a Testaccio
items.why: Since 1936 and open every day; the cacio e pepe is tossed at the table. A Sunday or Monday Testaccio lunch, 12:30 to 3:30.
items.quote: Open every day Lunch 12:30 PM - 3:30 PM

items.name: Antica Bottega del Vino
items.why: Verona's wine temple since 1890, open daily 11 am to 1 am; Amarone and Valpolicella by the glass after Perbellini.
items.quote: Un tempio del vino e del buon cibo, presente a Verona dal 1890

items.name: Torre dei Lamberti
items.why: Climb 289 steps or ride the glass elevator up Verona's 84 m tower for a 360 view; open every day. Walk off lunch here.
items.quote: La Torre dei Lamberti è visitabile tutti i giorni dell’anno (escluso 25 dicembre).

items.name: Mercato Albinelli
items.why: Liberty-style covered market from 1931, open Saturday 7 am to 7 pm; graze Parmigiano, balsamic and a Lambrusco before dinner.
items.quote: a covered market inaugurated in 1931 and still at the centre
